verdict.P1_specification_was_too_strict: REPORTED AS IT FELL. The pre-registered test asked for a strictly non-decreasing R-rate and Salmonella FAILS it on one dip: the 4-determinant stratum (n=14) sits below the 3-determinant one (n=17) with heavily overlapping Wilson intervals. The premise was 'R-rate rises with count'; strict monotonicity across small strata was a brittle way to operationalise it. The contrast below is the same premise without that brittleness, and it is reported BESIDE the failed test, not instead of it.

cross_organism_contrast.note: the SAME frozen rule (counter=qrdr_point, threshold=1) on the SAME drug. One QRDR hit predicts resistance in Campylobacter and does not in Salmonella, which is where the specificity gap between the two cells comes from.

mechanism_class_control.why: SAME organism, SAME cohort source, DIFFERENT rule shape. Salmonella x ceftriaxone uses subclass_any over ACQUIRED beta-lactamases; Salmonella x ciprofloxacin uses qrdr_point over TARGET-SITE point mutations. If the cipro over-call were a property of Salmonella labels or of this cohort, ceftriaxone would over-call too.
mechanism_class_control.reading: one ACQUIRED determinant is close to sufficient for ceftriaxone while one TARGET-SITE point mutation is close to uninformative for ciprofloxacin IN THE SAME ORGANISM AND COHORT, which exonerates the labels and the cohort: whatever is wrong is in the rule, not the data.
mechanism_class_control.the_acquired_vs_target_site_story_is_REF: The tempting generalisation -- threshold=1 suits acquired-enzyme mechanisms and mismatches target-site ones -- is WRONG, and the third cell is what kills it. Campylobacter ciprofloxacin is ALSO target-site (gyrA_T86I) and a single hit predicts at 0.9891. So mechanism CLASS does not decide it. What decides it is whether ONE determinant is clinically sufficient for that ORGANISM-DRUG PAIR: gyrA_T86I alone clears the Campylobacter cipro breakpoint, a single gyrA hit alone does not clear the Salmonella cipro breakpoint. threshold=1 is a claim about sufficiency per organism-drug pair, and it is a per-pair empirical question.

verdict.reading: The COUNT carries the information that presence does not FOR THIS PAIR: in Salmonella cipro a single counted determinant is almost always susceptible while two or more is usually resistant, so a threshold=1 rule over-calls by construction there. P2 true means parC's high PPV is parC MARKING a multi-hit genotype rather than predicting alone -- all parC carriers also carry gyrA -- so a rule that counted only parC would work for the wrong reason and would break on any population where parC arises first.

honest_limits: OBSERVATIONAL and MARGINAL: determinant count is not a causal dose. Carriers of 2 determinants differ from carriers of 1 in more than the count.
Determinant count is the count the FROZEN rule assigns, so it inherits whatever AMRFinder reports and whatever the rule's class filter admits -- not a complete genotype.
Reduced-susceptibility isolates sit near the breakpoint, so some S labels here are genuinely borderline; STRICT tiers reduce but do not remove that.
NOT clonality-corrected. A single-determinant stratum may be a few clones, and Salmonella surveillance is clonally structured.
This DIAGNOSES an over-call; it does not authorise a rule change. Changing what the frozen rule counts retires the active prospective lock and is a USER decision.
The two organisms' cohorts differ in source composition and size, so the Campylobacter arm is a CONTRAST, not a matched control.
